title: Reading a downloaded workflow before you run it
hook: A workflow file is data, and it can still cost you. Five things to look for before you press Queue, and where each one hides.

verified.claim: ComfyUI imports every custom node pack's code when it starts, with exec_module, and --disable-all-custom-nodes turns that off.
A class the server doesn't have gives missing_node_type, whose message says the custom node may not be installed.
Partner nodes live in comfy_api_nodes, object_info marks them api_node, and the help text calls them the paid API nodes. --disable-partner-nodes and --offline exist.
The workflow schema has an optional models list of name, url, hash, hash_type and directory, and definitions.subgraphs holds whole inner graphs.
verified.ref: docs.comfy.org/specs/workflow_json and front end workflowSchema.ts, fetched 2026-11-01

verified.claim: The editor allows model downloads only from civitai.com, civitai.red, huggingface.co and a few exact URLs, and only for .safetensors, .sft, .ckpt, .pth and .pt.
verified.ref: front end main branch, modelUrlAllowlist.ts and missingModelDownload.ts, fetched 2026-11-01

verified.claim: A save prefix that leaves the output folder is refused.
The docs say embedded metadata is optional, untrusted input and not a digital signature.
The practice graph passes validate_prompt and ran on a CPU.

unchecked: We have not audited every core node for what it can read or write. 'Core nodes are not a danger' is not a claim this lesson makes.
We read the download rules on the front end's main branch. Your version may differ, and tools outside the editor apply their own rules or none.
Pack managers are left out: we did not read how any of them installs a missing pack, so we say only that installing a pack means running its code.
We did not test what the editor shows for a workflow with missing nodes or a subgraph.
